column4: The Holy Spirit is not a new spirit but is of God and has been with God since the very beginning. In Genesis 1:2 the Spirit of God is hovering on the waters during creation. In Nehemiah 9:20, the scriptures say that it was the Spirit who instructed the people in the wilderness. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God anointed the kings, judges, and prophets in the Old Testament. In Joel 2:28-29 the Spirit is promised to be poured out on all mankind. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God raised Jesus from the dead, and now dwells in us (Romans 8:11). There is only one Holy Spirit, and He has always been the same. How He works with people has looked different at different times, but His heart has never changed.

column4: The Holy Spirit is first and foremost, from and of God. The scriptures refer to the Spirit as the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ, while these highlight different aspects, they are all one in the same. The Holy Spirit, being fully God, is also eternal and is holy (blameless, innocent, pure, not profane). Some translations refer to the Holy Spirit as the Holy Ghost.

Scripture calls the Spirit the Spirit of God, the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ; although these highlight different aspects, they are all the same. column4: The word spirit in Greek is **Pneuma** (**NYOO-mah** - **G4151**), it means breath, or wind. The Hebrew word for spirit means the same. Breath is significant as we need it in constant supply to live. It was God's breath that He blew into Adam to bring Him to life, likewise it was Jesus' breath that He breathed last before He died on the cross. Without breath there is no life. Breath like wind can be felt and experienced but are not as easily observed as other ‘elements’ water, fire, earth.
column5: In Greek, the word for “spirit” is **Pneuma** (**NYOO-mah** - **G4151**), which means breath or wind. The Hebrew word for “spirit” has the same meaning. Breath is important because we need its continual supply to live. God breathed His breath into Adam to give him life; likewise, the last breath Jesus took before dying on the cross was also breath. Without breath there is no life. Breath, like wind, can be felt and experienced, but it is not as easily seen as other “elements” like water, fire, or earth.

column4: > **<u>Matthew 16:18</u>** (NKJV)\\n>\\n> And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.\\n>
column5: > **<u>Matthew 16:18</u>** (NKJV)\\n>\\n> And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.\\n>

column4: This is an amazing and comforting promise. Gates are fixed defensive armaments. When Jesus says that the *gates of hell shall not prevail*, He is painting the picture of a conquering army that knocks down the gates and captures the city!
column5: This is a wonderful and comforting promise. Gates are stationary defensive structures. When Jesus says that *the gates of Hades shall not prevail*, He is painting a picture of a victorious army that knocks down the gates and takes the city!

column4: The Holy Spirit brings supernatural boldness to proclaim the witness of the Gospel in the face of persecution. The outcome of this empowerment can be described, but it's best experienced. It’s a supernatural (greater than human) boldness that motivates believers to share. This boldness of preaching is often accompanied by supernatural acts of demonstration of the Spirit and of power (1 Corinthians 2:1-5). People are healed physically and emotionally, the dead raised, those tormented by evil spirits are set free, people with hard hearts turn and repent.
column5: The Holy Spirit gives supernatural courage to proclaim the witness of the gospel in the face of persecution. The results of this empowerment can be described, but it is best experienced. It is a supernatural (beyond human) courage that compels believers to share. This boldness in preaching is often accompanied by supernatural works of demonstration of the Spirit and of power (1 Corinthians 2:1-5). People are healed physically and emotionally, the dead are raised, those oppressed by evil spirits are set free, the hard-hearted turn and repent.

column4: Jesus said these works and greater would we do! (John 14:12). These collective works are supernatural, divine, and desperately needed in a world tearing itself apart, miserable, full of pain, waiting for the mature sons of God to be made clearly manifest! (Romans 8:22-23)
column5: Jesus said that we will do these works and even greater ones! (John 14:12). These collective works are supernatural, divine, and in a world that is tearing itself apart, grieving, filled with suffering, and waiting for the clear revealing of the mature sons of God, they are desperately needed! (Romans 8:22-23)

column4: Jesus' chosen instrument for change on the earth is His church, empowered, emboldened, and directed by the Holy Spirit.
column5: The instrument Jesus has chosen for transformation on the earth is His church, empowered, emboldened, and guided by the Holy Spirit.

column4: ## Building a Relationship with the Holy Spirit
column5: ## Building a Relationship with the Holy Spirit

column4: Every relationship takes time and experience to develop deeply. The Holy Spirit is our advocate, our comforter, our helper, and our guide. He empowers us and sanctifies us.
column5: Every relationship takes time and experience to develop deeply. The Holy Spirit is our advocate, our comforter, our helper, and our guide. He empowers us and sanctifies us.

column4: Start to think of the Holy Spirit as you would a person. In our relationship we can both work to build it or do things that weaken our relationship. He can be ignored, He can be quenched, He can be blasphemed, or He can be listened to, honored, and obeyed.
column5: Begin to think of the Holy Spirit as a person. In our relationship, we can either work to build it or do things that weaken it. He can be ignored, quenched, blasphemed, or He can be listened to, honored, and obeyed.

column4: Don’t ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. He is always speaking to us and the church. If you don’t yet know how to distinguish the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, willingness, and effort (like all healthy and beneficial relationships). But don’t worry, you already have built into you all the necessary parts needed to start to develop a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit.
column5: Do not ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. He always speaks to us and to the Church. If you do not yet know how to distinguish the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, willingness, and effort (as in every healthy and beneficial relationship). But do not worry; within you are already all the necessary components needed to begin developing a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit.

column4: The quickest and most reliable ways to build an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit is to
column5: The fastest and most reliable ways to build an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit are

column4: 1.  Call out to Him **individually** in prayer, pause and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 1.  In prayer, call on Him **personally**, pause, and wait for Him to speak.

column4: 2.  Call out to Him as part of a **group** of people who know Him (the church), pause, and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 2.  As part of a **group** of those who know Him (the Church), call on Him, pause, and wait for Him to speak.

column4: I use the phrase ‘call out’ to mean literally, with your mouth, or however you speak (with your hands if you cannot speak aloud with your mouth). Why speak? A few reasons:
column5: I use the phrase ‘call out’ literally, to mean speaking with your mouth, or however you speak (with your hands if you cannot speak aloud with your mouth). Why speak? A few reasons:

column4: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in God's image. God speaks, and so do we.
column5: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in the image of God. God speaks, and we speak too.

column4: 2.  We use speaking as the primary way to communicate. You can also write down what you want to say (journaling) and speak it aloud.
column5: 2.  Speaking is the primary way we communicate. You can also write what you want to say (journaling) and speak it out loud.

column4: 3.  Speaking is an intentional act, and indicates to the party you are talking to, that you’d like to engage them in a conversation.
column5: 3.  Speaking is an intentional act, and it signals to the one you are addressing that you want to engage in conversation.

column4: #### What should you say?
column5: #### What should you say?

column4: If you’ve never talked to God, try introducing yourself. Sure, it will feel a bit weird, but that discomfort is okay and temporary. Along with introducing yourself, tell God that you want to talk to Him and that you want Him to talk back to you.
column5: If you have never spoken to God, try introducing yourself. Yes, it will feel a bit awkward, but that discomfort is okay and temporary. Along with your introduction, tell God that you want to talk with Him and that you want Him to talk with you as well.

column4: Consider asking Him a question. It doesn’t have to be a deep theological question; it can start simple. Can you show me Your love for me? Why do I have a certain feeling? What would You like to tell me?
column5: Consider asking Him a question. It does not have to be a deep theological question; it can start simple. Could You show me Your love for me? Why do I feel a certain way? What would You like to tell me?

column4: #### Then what?
column5: #### Then what?

column4: Well in all effective relationships you speak for a bit, then you pause and listen. God will speak.
column5: Well, in every effective relationship you speak for a while, then pause and listen. God will speak.

column4: God speaks in many ways, but He wants to do it personally, and internally. It will likely not be an audible voice (like if your best friend was to say your name aloud) but it will be an internal voice that speaks to your heart and mind. Elijah refers to this as the ‘still small voice’ (1 Kings 19:11-13).
column5: God speaks in many ways, but He wants to do it personally and inwardly. It will likely not be an audible voice (like your best friend saying your name out loud) but an inner voice that speaks to your heart and mind. Elijah calls it a ‘still small voice’ (1 Kings 19:11-13).

column4: The most common ways that I've personally witnessed God talk to people, and I've been blessed to help dozens of people learn how to talk to God directly, is some combination of the following:
column5: The most common ways in which I have personally seen God speak to people—and I have had the blessing of helping dozens of people learn to speak directly with God—are some combination of the following:

column4: - A knowing - the person talking to God gets an immediate understanding that helps them.
column5: - An insight - the person who is speaking with God immediately receives an understanding that helps them.

column4: - A picture - also known in the scriptures as a vision or a dream (a vision is when you are awake, a dream is when you are asleep), God will give you a picture in your mind. Perhaps it’s a memory, or place you’ve been or know? Explore the picture, what do you see? What do you feel as a result? What’s happening?
column5: - An image - also known in Scripture as a vision or a dream (a vision when you are awake, a dream when you are asleep), God will give an image in your mind. Perhaps it is a memory, or a place where you have been or that you know? Explore the image: what do you see? As a result what do you feel? What is happening?

column4: - An inner voice - like an audible voice, but one that only you can hear, and spoken into your heart and mind.
column5: - An inner voice - like an audible voice, but one that only you can hear, and which is spoken in your heart and mind.

column4: #### What will God say?
column5: #### What would God say?

column4: Not sure! But that’s the fun in it. I can say that He is NOT the spirit of fear, but of perfect love and that it will never violate the teaching of the scriptures. E.g., God will never tell you to commit an extra-marital affair.
column5: Not sure! But that’s the fun of it. I can say that He is not a spirit of fear, but of perfect love, and He will never violate the teaching of Scripture. e.g., God will never tell you to have an extramarital affair.

column4: Now what?
column5: Now what?

column4: Keep the dialogue going! It’s really that simple.
column5: Keep the conversation going! It really is that simple.

column4: ### Why build a relationship?
column5: ### Why build a relationship?

column4: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. The Helper helps us! The work goes much more smoothly if we have a shared language, and relationship with Him. Can you imagine trying to work with someone in your job if you had no relationship, did not speak the same language, and couldn't communicate?!
column5: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. The Helper helps us! If we have a shared language and relationship with Him, things go much more smoothly. Can you imagine trying to work on the job with someone with whom you have no relationship, you don’t speak the same language, and you can’t communicate?!

column4: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27), we have built into us all already the natural abilities we need, but we may lack experienced proficiency.
column5: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep recognize His voice (John 10:27), the natural capacities we need are already inherent within us, but it’s possible that we lack practiced proficiency.

column4: Speaking from personal experience, a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best things about being a Christian. His presence brings us peace, comfort, and direction, but only if you know how to seek, listen, and obey Him.
column5: From personal experience, having a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best things about being a Christian. His presence gives us peace, comfort, and direction, but only if you know how to seek Him, listen to Him, and obey Him.

column4: Develop a sensitivity with the Holy Spirit. Like many married people over time, you can communicate with your spouse in a unique way and sometimes just through a look. The look alone tells you everything you need to know about what just happened and what's going to happen. Build that type of sensitivity and familiarity with the Holy Spirit. Include Him in your whole life, this is a wonderful part of your relationship with Him that will provide so much depth and richness to your walk of faith.
column5: Develop a sensitivity to the Holy Spirit. Just as many married people, over time, are able to communicate with their spouse in a particular way—and sometimes with just a glance. That one glance tells you everything about what just happened and what’s about to happen. Build that same kind of sensitivity and familiarity with the Holy Spirit. Involve Him in your whole life; this is a wonderful part of your relationship with Him that will add great depth and richness to your walk of faith.

column4: The Holy Spirit has come to lead us and guide us, to empower us to be God’s people, and to see the people of the Earth radically transformed, delivered from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light. Getting to know him, building trust with Him is essential to everyday life and to accomplish the work that Jesus has for us to do.
column5: The Holy Spirit has come to lead and guide us, to empower us to become God’s people, and to see the people of the earth fully transformed and delivered from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light. Knowing Him, and building trust with Him, is essential for daily life and for accomplishing the work Jesus has given us to do.

column5: Our discussion of the work of the Holy Spirit does not conclude in this chapter. His work is discussed in detail in the remaining chapters of this book, especially in the chapters on sanctification and baptism.

column4: ## Personal Reflection Questions
column5: ## Personal reflection questions

column4: 1.  How have you experienced the Holy Spirit as your Comforter, Guide, or source of power? Which role resonates most with your current season of life?
column5: 1.  How have you experienced the Holy Spirit as your Comforter, Guide, or source of power? Which of these roles resonates most in your current season of life?

column4: 2.  Reflect on the difference between the Holy Spirit being “within” (inward work) and “upon” (outward work). How does this distinction impact your understanding of His work in your life?
column5: 2.  Reflect on the difference between the Holy Spirit being “within” (internal work) and “upon” (external work). How does this distinction affect your understanding of His work in your life?

column4: 3.  What steps can you take to cultivate a deeper relationship with the Holy Spirit and recognize His voice more clearly?
column5: 3.  What steps can you take to develop a deeper relationship with the Holy Spirit and to recognize His voice more clearly?

column4: 4.  We are to rely on the Holy Spirit’s power to step out in boldness and fulfill the mission God has given us. What specific mission and focus has God given you?
column5: 4.  We must boldly move forward and rely on the power of the Holy Spirit to fulfill the mission God has given. What specific mission and focus area has God given you?

column4: 5.  The Holy Spirit leads us into truth and discernment. Are there areas of your life where you need clarity or wisdom? How can you invite Him to guide you?
column5: 5.  The Holy Spirit leads us toward truth and discernment. Are there areas in your life where you need clarity or wisdom? How can you invite Him to guide you?

column4: ## Group Discussion Questions (20-30 Minutes)
column5: ## Group Discussion Questions (20-30 minutes)

column4: 1.  **Icebreaker Question:** “When you think of the Holy Spirit, what is the first word or image that comes to mind? Why?”
column5: 1.  **Icebreaker Question:** “When you think about the Holy Spirit, what is the first word or image that comes to mind? Why?”

column4: 2. **Exploring Scripture:** Read John 14:26. How does the Holy Spirit’s role as Teacher and Helper encourage you in your faith journey?
column5: 2. **Exploring Scripture:** Read John 14:26. How does the role of the Holy Spirit as Teacher and Helper encourage you in your journey of faith?

column4: 3.  **Holy Spirit Within vs. Upon:** Discuss the difference between the Holy Spirit being “within” for transformation and “upon” for empowerment. Why are both aspects essential for a believer?
column5: 3.  **Holy Spirit within vs. upon:** Discuss the difference between the Holy Spirit being “within” for transformation and “upon” for empowerment. Why are both aspects necessary for a believer?

column4: 4.  **Practical Guidance:** What are practical ways we can position ourselves to hear the Holy Spirit’s voice and follow His leading in daily decisions?
column5: 4.  **Practical guidance:** What practical ways can we position ourselves so that we can hear the Holy Spirit’s voice and follow His leading in daily decisions?

column4: 5.  **Reflection**: Think of a time when you felt empowered by the Holy Spirit to act. How did that experience impact your faith and the people around you?
column5: 5.  **Reflection**: Think about a time when you felt empowered by the Holy Spirit to take action. What impact did that experience have on your faith and on the people around you?
